criteria.description: The module defines model and path constants at module scope (mirroring the existing coverage modules' naming conventions) as named, monkeypatchable constants, plus a named LOOKBACK_WINDOW constant defaulting to 4 turns. LOOKBACK_WINDOW carries an explanatory docstring/comment stating it is load-bearing (explanations span turn boundaries) — it is a real named constant, not an inline magic number.

A hermetic test monkeypatches LOOKBACK_WINDOW at a MID-TRANSCRIPT position (first new turn well clear of the head clamp, i.e. first_new_index strictly greater than any window value under test) and asserts: (a) the number of preceding (lookback) turns selected by the pure request-assembly function equals min(LOOKBACK_WINDOW, first_new_index); (b) raising LOOKBACK_WINDOW selects STRICTLY MORE preceding turns at that mid-transcript position where the head clamp is not in play; (c) the upper bound holds — no selected preceding turn has an index below 0 and the count never exceeds the number of available preceding turns. Model/path constants are only required to be present and monkeypatchable (no live effect exercised this sprint).

criteria.description: The public contract for a single incremental pass is documented (docstring on the entry function plus a typed result structure, e.g. a dataclass) and stable in shape. INPUTS: session turns so far, index of last-judged turn, set of already-covered claim ids, full claim map, and a prompt passed as a versioned parameter (prompt text + version identifier) — the prompt is never hardcoded in the module. OUTPUTS: newly-covered claim ids each with per-claim evidence (cited turn indices + reason), the new last-judged-turn index, the prompt version used, and cost/usage for the pass. This entry path is exercised THIS sprint via an injected fake client (reusing the existing CountingClient/UsageTally style seam); only the real Anthropic transport path and credentialed smoke are deferred.
criteria.verifyBy: Grader reads the entry function signature and docstring / result dataclass confirming all named inputs and outputs are present. A hermetic test with an injected fake client asserts the returned object exposes: newly-covered claim ids, per-claim evidence with cited turns and reason, new last-judged-turn index, the recorded prompt version, and cost/usage fields.

criteria.description: Request-assembly logic — deciding which turns and which claims get sent to the model — is a pure, client-free, I/O-free function testable with no model call. The index space is pinned and documented: the last-judged index and the lookback arithmetic operate in the same turn-index space established by coverage_judge.load_transcript (the committed fixtures are contiguous 0-based, so list position and Turn.index coincide there). Window semantics: it selects all new turns (strictly after the last-judged index) PLUS exactly LOOKBACK_WINDOW turns immediately preceding the first new turn, clamped at the transcript start (index 0) so a near-head pass never under-runs the list; and it excludes every claim already in the covered set from what is sent.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests call the pure assembly function directly (no client) and assert: (a) turns sent = new turns plus exactly LOOKBACK_WINDOW preceding turns, clamped at 0 at the transcript head (explicit head-boundary test with last-judged index near 0, asserting count = min(LOOKBACK_WINDOW, first_new_index)); (b) claims sent exclude all ids in the covered set; (c) zero new turns selects no work; (d) all claims covered selects no claims; (e) a c49-shaped distributed-explanation test in which a cited prior turn lies strictly MORE than 1 and AT MOST 4 turns before the first new turn (mirroring the real c49 [4,6,8,14,16] straddle with unrelated turns in between): a window of 1 MISSES that prior turn while LOOKBACK_WINDOW=4 CATCHES it, pinning that 4 specifically is load-bearing. Grader confirms the function takes no client parameter, performs no I/O, and that the documented index space matches load_transcript.

criteria.description: Zero-work passes cost nothing OBSERVABLY, and malformed/failed passes degrade to nothing — both without mutating caller inputs. (i) A pass over zero new turns, and a pass where every claim is already covered, each perform NO model call and return empty additions with a zero/absent usage tally — the 'costs nothing' thesis is tied to an observable call count, not merely a present cost field. (ii) A malformed or failed fake-client response during an otherwise-non-trivial pass yields NO newly-covered claim ids (empty additions) and leaves the caller's inputs untouched — the covered set is not shrunk and not grown, and the turns list and claim map are unmutated — with no crash and no partial result. criteria.description: Turn identity throughout all sent-turn-set assertions is 0-BASED ARRAY POSITION in the transcript's turns list (the fixtures carry no index field; this basis is fixed by fiat for this module). A single incremental pass judges exactly the NEW turns (array positions after the last-judged-turn index J, i.e. positions J+1..N where N is the last position) PLUS a lookback of `window` turns extending BACKWARD from the first new turn — i.e. the request turn set is positions max(0, J+1-window)..N inclusive, where `window` defaults to LOOKBACK_WINDOW==4. Boundary behavior is pinned: clamped at 0 when fewer than `window` prior turns exist (no negative index) and a mid-session case.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with an injected fake client that captures the request; assert the captured 0-based turn positions equal an expected list that is DERIVED FROM the module's LOOKBACK_WINDOW constant and J (e.g. `list(range(max(0, J+1-mod.LOOKBACK_WINDOW), N+1))`), NOT two independent hand-written literals, so that changing LOOKBACK_WINDOW to 3 or 5 changes the expected list and breaks the test. Cover (a) a start-of-transcript case where the lower bound clamps to 0, and (b) a mid-session case with J>=window so the lower bound is exactly J+1-window. A wrong direction or off-by-one slice must fail.

criteria.description: A c49-shaped distributed-explanation test proves the lookback is load-bearing at the TURN-SET level (not by any verdict, which c8 forbids) using the default window (4). A synthetic transcript is constructed with a distributed explanation whose cited evidence occupies real 0-based positions [4,6,8,14,16], with the first new turn at position 15 (last-judged J=14). The default-window lower bound is max(0,15-4)=11, so the reachable range is positions 11..N inclusive. The default-window request MUST send EXACTLY that turn set; the reachable set therefore INCLUDES the in-reach cited positions {14,16} and EXCLUDES the out-of-reach cited positions {4,6,8}. A companion pass with window=0 (override, per c1) MUST show position 14 absent — demonstrating the reachable evidence set differs from the naive window by exactly the lookback.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserting against the fake client's captured request that under the default window the sent 0-based turn set EQUALS the literal expected list range(11, N+1) (with the cited positions [4,6,8,14,16] being genuine positions in the synthetic transcript), and as corollaries is a superset of {14,16} and disjoint from {4,6,8}; under an explicit window=0 pass (override parameter from c1, not monkeypatching) the sent turn set does not contain 14. No coverage verdict is asserted — only turn-set membership.

criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts the return value exposes (a) the final covered-id set and (b) per-pass usage sequences (per_pass_calls, per_pass_input_tokens, per_pass_output_tokens) whose lengths each equal run.passes (a single scalar total does NOT satisfy this), each element an int, plus per-pass newly-covered ids; assert these fields are sufficient to derive a dollar cost (e.g., via the module's existing usage/tally helper) without further model calls.

criteria.description: Monotonic accumulation across the simulation loop: the caller-owned covered set only grows pass over pass — never shrinks and never drops a previously-covered id — and equals the union of all per-pass additions at the end.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with a fake client returning staged coverage across passes asserts len(covered) is non-decreasing at every step and that final covered == union of all per-pass additions with no duplicates or losses.

criteria.description: Per-pass REQUEST SIZE — not merely call count — stays flat as the session lengthens: for each pass the driver sends only that pass's new turns (bounded by the cadence) plus the fixed lookback window, and only candidate (not-yet-covered) claims. In particular the FIRST pass must NOT send the entire transcript — it too is bounded by (cadence + LOOKBACK_WINDOW). Over a multi-pass simulation of the 159-turn long fixture, turns-per-request is bounded by (cadence + LOOKBACK_WINDOW) for EVERY pass including the first, and candidate-claims-per-request is non-increasing pass-over-pass, with at least one pass where the candidate-claims count strictly decreases after claims become covered (proving exclusion actually shrinks the payload, not merely that it never grows on a degenerate all-uncovered run).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test drives simulate_incremental_run over the 159-turn fixture with an injected fake client that records each outbound request. Request payloads are inspected via the INJECTED FAKE CLIENT's recorded calls (e.g. client.calls), NOT via SimulatedRun (which does not carry requests), using the harness request-payload helpers (_sent_turn_positions_from_request / _sent_claim_ids); the test associates recorded calls with passes correctly, expecting NO recorded request for zero-work / fully-covered passes. It asserts: the FIRST recorded request's turns-count <= cadence + LOOKBACK_WINDOW (explicitly NOT ~159); every recorded request's turns-count <= cadence + LOOKBACK_WINDOW; candidate-claims-count non-increasing across recorded requests; and >=1 recorded request where candidate-claims-count strictly decreases relative to an earlier one. The assertions read captured request payloads, NOT per_pass_calls.

criteria.description: Correct exclusion is preserved ACROSS the loop, not just within a single pass: once the accumulating covered set grows, every accumulated covered id is absent from every later pass's candidate-claim request payload. Covered claims are never re-sent to 'catch up'.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test drives simulate_incremental_run (>=3 passes over the long fixture) with a fake that covers claims on early passes and records its outbound requests. Using the injected fake client's recorded calls (client.calls) — NOT SimulatedRun — and the harness helper _sent_claim_ids, it captures each later pass's candidate-claim payload (skipping passes with no recorded request) and asserts every id in the accumulated covered set at the start of a pass does not appear in that pass's candidate set.

criteria.description: Windowing is honored by the loop (lookback carried through, not widened): each pass judges new turns plus the fixed lookback window into prior turns, and the window is the module's named, documented, monkeypatchable parameter (LOOKBACK_WINDOW, resolved at call time) — the driver must not widen it or add any re-judge of covered claims to close the under-credit gap.
criteria.verifyBy: Read the driver: it passes the module's named window parameter through unchanged and has no code path that re-sends covered claims. Hermetic test drives the 159-turn fixture at a concrete, named cadence (turns_per_pass=8) chosen so an interior full-width pass is guaranteed reachable; asserts turns-count <= turns_per_pass + LOOKBACK_WINDOW for every recorded request and equals turns_per_pass + LOOKBACK_WINDOW for at least one interior pass where the head-clamp is not active; asserts the window resolves to LOOKBACK_WINDOW at call time (default 4) and honors monkeypatching of that constant.

criteria.description: Zero-work boundaries hold in the loop: a pass over zero new turns performs no model call and adds nothing; a run where every claim is already covered performs no further model calls; a cadence that overshoots the end of the transcript terminates cleanly without error.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests assert the fake client is not called for empty-turn or fully-covered passes and that the simulation terminates at end-of-transcript with the fake client call count matching only the non-empty, non-exhausted passes.

criteria.description: Failure of a single pass MID-SIMULATION degrades to nothing: when one pass inside simulate_incremental_run raises or returns malformed output, that pass adds nothing, the accumulated covered set after it equals the set before it (never shrunk, never partial), the failure is recorded (e.g., in run.errors) and logged, no exception propagates out of the loop, and a subsequent pass still runs and can still add coverage.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test injects a fake client that fails (raises or returns malformed output) on exactly one mid-run pass of simulate_incremental_run and asserts: covered-after == covered-before for that failed pass (the covered set did NOT advance across the failure); run.errors records the error; no exception propagates; and a later pass still adds ids. Non-vacuity: the test would fail if merge-on-failure regressed or if the failure aborted the loop. The failure is exercised inside the loop, not by calling run_incremental_pass directly.

criteria.description: A measurability helper exposes the under-credit gap: given a simulated incremental covered-id set and a full-transcript teardown covered-id set for the same session, it computes the difference (ids the incremental run missed, any extra ids, counts, and/or a covered ratio) so the gap can be measured on real data — pure, no I/O required to compute the diff.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test feeds a known incremental set and a known teardown set and asserts the helper reports the missing ids (and extras) and the size of the gap correctly, including the equal-sets (zero gap) case and the incremental-subset-of-teardown case.

Confirm by inspection that the c4/c5/c8 tests read captured request payloads from the injected fake client / mid-loop failure state (not per_pass_calls alone), so they would fail against a driver that sends the whole transcript on pass 1, or lacks exclusion, flat windowing, or failure isolation.

scope.description: No pipeline wiring: bot.py, session lifecycle, frontend, and any Pipecat imports remain untouched. This sprint adds only a pure driver/helper and its tests.
Do not author, tune, or hardcode the judge prompt; the prompt stays a versioned INPUT threaded through unchanged. No chasing specific coverage verdict numbers as acceptance.
Do not widen the lookback window or add any re-examination of already-covered claims to close the under-credit gap — only make the gap observable/measurable.
~/.voice-tutor/ is strictly read-only and is NOT touched by the hermetic layer at all; any real-data reads belong only to a credentialed smoke path that skips cleanly without a key and never writes.
Do not change teardown judging (it stays the strict record and only sidecar writer), do not persist live state (in-memory, caller-owned), and add no new dependencies or venvs.
Changes confined to the coverage module lane and its tests (alongside coverage_judge.py / coverage_store.py and tests/fixtures/coverage/); do not rewrite unrelated modules.
